rows.notes: The study is a systematic literature review (24 selected peer-reviewed articles on adoption of drip irrigation in India, 2001-2018); it reports no primary data, experiment, survey or model runs of its own. On the claim (water and fertiliser saving while maintaining profitability), the review in fact argues the opposite of the passage: it states that mere adoption of micro-irrigation does not result in water conservation at farm level because farmers expand irrigated area, raise cropping intensity or shift to water-intensive crops (rebound effect), and that plot-level efficiency gains cannot be extrapolated to the farm. Water/fertiliser/energy savings and cost reductions mentioned are cited from other studies (Narayanamoorthy 2004b; Kumar 2012; Reddy 2016 etc.), not the review's own results.

notes: Document is a complete systematic literature review article (Development in Practice 33(1):76-86); Q1 is 'no' so all other questions are 'no'. The review's main conclusions (subsidies alone insufficient for adoption; adoption does not automatically conserve water) partly contradict the direction of the cited claim.
